PhILR Distance

Source: R/philr.r
philr_distance.Rd

Euclidean distances between samples' PhILR coordinates, with the weights that Silverman et al. (2017) recommend: a compositional, phylogenetic beta diversity.

Usage

philr_distance(
  counts,
  tree = NULL,
  margin = 1L,
  pseudocount = NULL,
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of counts or proportions (samples \(\times\) features, see margin), or an object of one of the types in Input Types. Its features must have names, matched to the tips of tree. The part weights assume counts.

tree

A phylo object with branch lengths, whose tips include every feature of counts, or NULL to use the tree inside counts (a phyloseq, rbiom or TreeSummarizedExperiment object, or attr(counts, 'tree')).

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

pseudocount

Added to every value before taking logs. NULL (the default) adds nothing when counts has no zeros, and otherwise uses half the smallest non-zero value, with a warning. See Pseudocount.

pairs

Which combinations of samples should distances be calculated for? The default value (NULL) calculates all-vs-all. Provide a numeric or logical vector specifying positions in the distance matrix to calculate. See examples.

clust

Whether and how to cluster the samples (rows and columns) before returning the distance matrix: NULL (the default) or FALSE to keep them in their input order, or one of stats::hclust()'s linkage methods, "average" (UPGMA), "complete", "single", "ward.D", "ward.D2", "mcquitty" (WPGMA), "median" or "centroid", or "pcoa" to order them along the first axis of pcoa(). Clustering reorders the samples of the result, with their labels (samples without names are labelled with their positions in the input): its dist record (see ecodive_steps) gives each one's position in the input as order, so that meta[attr(d, "dist")$order, ] lines metadata up with them. ecodive's ordinations and tests put the samples back in their input order before analysing them, so give them metadata in its usual order. Other packages see the reordered matrix: give them metadata reordered by order, or matched by name. The record's clust records clust (FALSE as "none"), which plot.ecodive_dist() follows: with NULL it clusters the samples for the heatmap ("average"), and with "none" it keeps their order. clust needs every distance, so it cannot be used with pairs. rho_p()'s similarities are clustered as \(1 - \rho_p\).

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), will use all logical CPU cores.

Value

A distance matrix: a dist object of class c("ecodive_dist", "dist"), as every metric function returns (see beta_div()).

Details

The distance between samples \(x\) and \(y\) is $$\sqrt{\sum_i \left(x^*_i - y^*_i\right)^2},$$ where \(x^*\) are the philr() coordinates of \(x\) with part weights 'enorm.x.gm.counts' and ILR weights 'blw.sqrt' (Silverman et al. 2017, Methods), so that

philr_distance(x, tree) ==
  euclidean(philr(x, tree, part_weights = 'enorm.x.gm.counts', ilr_weights = 'blw.sqrt'))

For other weightings, use euclidean(philr(x, tree, ...)). With uniform weights, PhILR distances are Aitchison distances (aitchison()): the weights are what make them phylogenetic. The part weights are computed from all the samples, so adding or removing a sample changes the distances between the others. pairs limits which distances are computed, not the samples used.

The tree is handled as philr() handles it: tips that aren't features are dropped, and polytomies are resolved, with a warning (see The tree in philr()). It needs branch lengths.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

Pseudocount

Logs of zero are undefined, so zeros need replacing first. The pseudocount is added to every value (not only to zeros), as in normalize(norm = 'clr'). With pseudocount = NULL (the default), no pseudocount is used when counts has no zeros; otherwise half the smallest non-zero value is, with a warning. To avoid a pseudocount, replace the zeros first with replace_zeros(): its result has none.

The choice of pseudocount is not neutral: it can distort the results, especially for sparse tables. See aitchison() for references.

References

Silverman, J. D., Washburne, A. D., Mukherjee, S., & David, L. A. (2017). A phylogenetic transform enhances analysis of compositional microbiota data. eLife, 6, e21887. doi:10.7554/eLife.21887

See also

philr(), beta_div(), aitchison(), weighted_unifrac()

Other Phylogenetic metrics: faith(), generalized_unifrac(), normalized_unifrac(), unweighted_unifrac(), variance_adjusted_unifrac(), weighted_unifrac()

Examples

    philr_distance(ex_counts, tree = ex_tree, pseudocount = 1)
#>          Saliva      Gums      Nose
#> Gums   45.35818                    
#> Nose  174.56795 173.14851          
#> Stool 280.52778 262.97008 182.59416

    # The same, from beta_div()
    d <- beta_div(ex_counts, 'philr', tree = ex_tree, pseudocount = 1)
